project.name: duo
project.tagline: A permanent video room for exactly two people.
core_constraints: Exactly two participants — ever. No rooms, no lobbies, no meeting IDs.
Peer-to-peer WebRTC by default; TURN relay fallback only when ICE direct paths fail.
UI must visibly indicate connection type ('direct' vs 'relayed') in subtle text.
Self-hosted Node.js signaling server, exposed via ngrok during development.
Reuse battle-tested libraries (simple-peer, coturn, ws) instead of hand-rolling WebRTC/STUN/TURN.
non_features_explicitly_omitted: Room creation / room listing / room IDs
User search, friend lists, contact directory
Group chat, breakout rooms, screen-share moderation
Account signup flows beyond a single pre-shared pair credential

system_architecture.pattern: Two-peer WebRTC mesh (which for N=2 is just one bidirectional peer connection) with a thin always-on signaling broker. The broker is stateless beyond a single in-memory PairState singleton — because there is only ever one pair, there is no room table, no lookup, no GC.
system_architecture.topology_diagram_ascii:
[Peer A browser] <==DTLS/SRTP P2P==> [Peer B browser]
        \                                    /
         \---WSS signaling---> [Server] <---WSS signaling---/
                                  |
                                  +-- [coturn STUN/TURN :3478/:5349]

components.name: web-client
components.type: Static SPA (Vite + vanilla TS, no framework — two-user UI is too small to justify React)
responsibilities: Render local + remote video, mute/cam controls, connection-type indicator
Authenticate to signaling server with the pair's shared secret

components.name: signaling-server
components.type: Node.js 20 + ws (WebSocket) + express (only for /health and serving static client)
responsibilities: Accept exactly two authenticated WebSocket connections at a time (slot A, slot B)
Relay SDP offer/answer and ICE candidates between the two slots
Mint short-lived TURN credentials (HMAC-SHA1 over username, RFC 5766 / coturn 'use-auth-secret' mode)
Expose ICE server config to clients at /ice-config
Broadcast presence (other peer online/offline) immediately on connect/disconnect

components.name: coturn
components.type: External binary, run via Docker (coturn/coturn image)
components.runtime: Same host as signaling-server (colocated for simplicity)
responsibilities: TURN relay for symmetric-NAT / restrictive-firewall fallback
Authenticate clients via shared static-auth-secret (REST API per RFC 5766) so credentials can rotate without restart

server.store: Single in-memory module-scoped singleton named PairState. No database — losing it on restart is fine; users just reconnect.
server.shape: PairState = { slots: [SlotState | null, SlotState | null] } where SlotState = { ws: WebSocket, peerId: 'A' | 'B', connectedAt: number, lastPongAt: number }
invariants: slots.length === 2 always (positions are stable, not a list)
A given authenticated identity always occupies the same slot (A or B is derived from the credential, not from arrival order)
If a third client authenticates successfully, it BUMPS the existing occupant of its slot (so reconnects after network blips just work) — never accepted as a third party

client.store: Single Zustand-like vanilla store (custom 30-line implementation in lib/store.ts). No Redux.
client.shape: ClientState = { phase: 'idle'|'connecting-signal'|'waiting-for-peer'|'negotiating'|'connected'|'reconnecting'|'failed', localStream: MediaStream|null, remoteStream: MediaStream|null, micMuted: boolean, camOff: boolean, connectionType: 'direct'|'relayed'|'unknown', lastError: string|null }

happy_path: 1. Peer A loads SPA. Client reads pair-secret from URL fragment (#k=...) or localStorage; if absent, shows a one-input 'paste your pair key' screen.
2. Client GETs /ice-config (returns STUN + ephemeral TURN credentials).
3. Client calls getUserMedia({video, audio}); on grant, opens WSS to /signal with Authorization: Bearer <pair-secret>.
4. Server validates credential -> derives slot (A or B) -> places ws in PairState.slots[slot]. Sends { type: 'hello', you: 'A', peerPresent: true|false }.

5. Designated initiator (slot A) waits for { type: 'peer-joined' } from server, then constructs simple-peer({ initiator: true, stream: localStream, config: iceConfig }). Slot B constructs with initiator:false.
6. simple-peer emits 'signal' events (SDP/ICE); client forwards each as { type: 'signal', data } over WS. Server forwards to the other slot verbatim.

7. Once both peers ICE-connected, peerconnection.getStats() is polled once; selected candidate-pair's 'remote-candidate.candidateType' === 'relay' -> connectionType='relayed', else 'direct'. Updated in store, rendered as small footer text.
8. Steady state: media flows P2P (or via TURN). Signaling WS remains open but idle — used only for renegotiation, hangup, and presence.
data_flow.renegotiation: On track add/remove (e.g. screen-share toggle), simple-peer fires 'signal' again; same forwarding path. No special server logic.
data_flow.reconnect: If the WS drops, client retries with exponential backoff (250ms -> 4s, capped). If the WebRTC datachannel/media drops but WS is up, the initiator triggers ICE restart (simple-peer.send empty / pc.restartIce()) after 3s grace.
data_flow.hangup: Client sends { type: 'bye' }; server forwards. Both clients tear down peer connection but keep WS open (presence stays online).

shared_types_typescript.IceServerConfig: interface IceServerConfig { iceServers: RTCIceServer[]; ttlSeconds: number }
shared_types_typescript.SignalEnvelope: type SignalEnvelope = HelloMsg | PeerJoinedMsg | PeerLeftMsg | SignalMsg | ByeMsg | PingMsg | PongMsg | ErrorMsg
shared_types_typescript.HelloMsg: interface HelloMsg { type: 'hello'; you: PeerId; peerPresent: boolean; serverTime: number }
shared_types_typescript.SignalMsg: interface SignalMsg { type: 'signal'; data: unknown /* opaque simple-peer payload */ }
shared_types_typescript.ErrorMsg: interface ErrorMsg { type: 'error'; code: 'unauthorized' | 'malformed' | 'rate-limited'; message: string }

pair_secret.purpose: Single long-lived shared secret that authorizes this exact pair. There is no user database; the secret IS the identity.
pair_secret.generation: Server bootstraps with PAIR_SECRET_A and PAIR_SECRET_B env vars (two distinct base64url 32-byte strings). Each peer holds one. Whichever secret you present determines whether you occupy slot A or B.
pair_secret.transport: HTTP `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` for /ice-config and WSS Sec-WebSocket-Protocol subprotocol value `bearer.<secret>` for /signal (browsers can't set headers on WS).
pair_secret.rotation: Operator edits env vars and restarts. Clients then re-paste secret. No rotation flow needed in v1.

data_models.no_persistent_storage: There are no database tables. No users, no messages, no call history. All state is in-memory and ephemeral. This is intentional — the spec is 'two people, always connected, no record'.

repo_layout./: Monorepo root. Two packages, no workspaces tool — just two folders with their own package.json (kept dead-simple).
repo_layout./docker-compose.yml: Brings up server + coturn together for local dev
repo_layout./README.md: Operator setup: generate secrets, run docker-compose up, run ngrok http 8080, paste URL into both peers' browsers

server_modules.purpose: Process entrypoint. Boots HTTP server, mounts /health, /ice-config, /signal (WebSocket upgrade), serves /client static build.
Reads + validates env vars at startup. Fails fast if any required var missing.
exports: const config: { port: number; pairSecretA: string; pairSecretB: string; turnStaticAuthSecret: string; turnRealm: string; publicTurnHost: string; publicTurnPort: number; turnTcpPort: number; turnsTlsPort: number }
validation_rules: PAIR_SECRET_A and PAIR_SECRET_B must each be >= 32 chars and must differ
Process exits with code 1 and a clear error if any fail

server_modules.purpose: Constant-time credential compare. Maps presented secret -> PeerId | null.
exports: function timingSafeEqual(a: string, b: string): boolean
implementation_notes: Uses crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length Buffers; returns false for mismatched lengths.
Never logs the secret itself; logs only which slot was identified.

server_modules.purpose: The singleton in-memory pair state. Owns slot assignment, bump-on-reconnect, and message routing.
exports: function attach(peerId: 'A'|'B', ws: WebSocket): { replaced: boolean }
function detach(peerId: 'A'|'B', ws: WebSocket): void  /* no-op if ws no longer current */
behavior_contract: attach('A', ws2) when slots[0] already holds ws1: send { type:'error', code:'replaced' } to ws1, close it with code 4000, then install ws2. Returns { replaced: true }.
detach is idempotent and only clears the slot if the provided ws is the current occupant (handles late close events after a replace).

server_modules.purpose: WebSocket upgrade handler. Parses subprotocol auth, attaches to PairState, relays SignalEnvelope between slots.
behavior_contract: On upgrade: extract subprotocol matching `bearer.<secret>`; reject with 401 if missing/invalid.
After attach: send HelloMsg to new socket; if peer present, send PeerJoinedMsg to BOTH sockets.
On message: validate via envelope.parse; if 'signal' or 'bye', forward to otherSocket; if 'ping', reply 'pong' from server (does not cross peers); else send ErrorMsg.
Heartbeat: server ping every 20s; if no pong in 45s, terminate ws.
Rate limit: max 100 messages/second per socket (token bucket). Excess -> ErrorMsg + close 4001.

server_modules.purpose: Zod schemas for SignalEnvelope variants; parse() returns typed message or throws.
implementation_notes: Reject messages > 16 KiB (SDP fits comfortably under this; anything larger is suspect).
`signal.data` is z.unknown() — opaque passthrough, since it's just simple-peer payload.

server_modules.purpose: Mints ICE server config (STUN + ephemeral TURN creds) on each request.
exports: function mountIceConfigRoute(app: express.Express): void  /* requires Authorization: Bearer <pair-secret> */
implementation_notes: Returns iceServers: [{ urls: 'stun:<host>:3478' }, { urls: ['turn:<host>:3478?transport=udp','turn:<host>:3478?transport=tcp','turns:<host>:5349?transport=tcp'], username, credential }], ttlSeconds: 600.
Route is GET, requires Authorization header bearer-equal to one of the pair secrets; rate-limited (10 req / minute / IP).

server_modules.returns: 200 OK { ok: true, peerA: boolean, peerB: boolean, uptimeSeconds: number }

client_modules.purpose: Single page. Body contains <video id='remote' autoplay playsinline></video>, <video id='local' autoplay playsinline muted></video>, controls bar, footer indicator span.
App entrypoint. Wires phase machine, mounts UI handlers, kicks off connect flow.
Resolves the pair secret from URL fragment (#k=...) > localStorage > prompt UI. Persists to localStorage on first paste.
implementation_notes: URL fragment is preferred because fragments are never sent to the server in HTTP requests (the secret lives only in the browser).
After reading from #k=, the fragment is cleared from the address bar via history.replaceState.

client_modules.purpose: Minimal reactive store (30 LOC) — { state, set(patch), subscribe(fn) }.
exports: const store: { get(): ClientState; set(patch: Partial<ClientState>): void; subscribe(fn: (s: ClientState) => void): () => void }

client_modules.purpose: Wraps getUserMedia + track enable/disable for mute/cam.
exports: function setMicMuted(stream: MediaStream, muted: boolean): void
function setCamOff(stream: MediaStream, off: boolean): void

client_modules.purpose: WebSocket client. Connects with subprotocol auth, exposes typed emitter for incoming envelopes, send() for outgoing.
exports: interface SignalClient { onMessage(fn: (msg: SignalEnvelope) => void): void; send(msg: SignalEnvelope): void; close(): void; readonly state: 'connecting'|'open'|'closing'|'closed'|'reconnecting' }
function connectSignal(opts: { url: string; pairSecret: string }): SignalClient
implementation_notes: Drops any buffered outgoing messages on reconnect — caller (rtcSession) re-emits as needed.

client_modules.purpose: Owns the simple-peer instance. Wires its 'signal' events to signalClient.send and incoming SignalMsgs into peer.signal(). Detects connection type after ICE connected.
exports: interface RtcSession { destroy(): void; restartIce(): void }
function startRtcSession(opts: { initiator: boolean; localStream: MediaStream; iceConfig: IceServerConfig; signal: SignalClient }): RtcSession
implementation_notes: Connection-type detection: after peer.on('connect'), poll peer._pc.getStats(); find report where type='candidate-pair' and selected===true (Chrome) or use the report with state='succeeded' and nominated===true; then look up its remoteCandidateId; that report's candidateType === 'relay' -> 'relayed', else 'direct'. Update store.
Re-runs detection on iceconnectionstatechange='connected' transitions (covers ICE restarts).

client_modules.purpose: Pure DOM bindings: subscribes to store and writes to elements; reads control clicks and dispatches actions.
exports: function mountUi(handlers: { onMicToggle(): void; onCamToggle(): void; onHangup(): void }): void
ui_contract: Remote video fills viewport. Local video is a draggable PiP in bottom-right (CSS only, no JS drag lib needed beyond pointer events).
Controls bar: mic toggle, cam toggle, hangup. Visible only on pointer movement; auto-fade after 3s idle.
Footer (bottom-center, font-size: 11px, opacity: 0.55): renders connectionType — 'direct' | 'relayed via TURN' | reconnecting state.
Phase 'waiting-for-peer' shows centered text: 'Waiting for the other one.' — no progress spinner, no instructions.
Phase 'failed' shows centered text + a 'try again' button that re-runs bootstrap().

client_modules.purpose: Fetches /ice-config with bearer auth and caches per ttl.
exports: async function fetchIceConfig(opts: { baseUrl: string; pairSecret: string }): Promise<IceServerConfig>

coturn_module.purpose: Coturn config tuned for two-user fixed-credential pair.
key_directives: total-quota=4  (two pairs of relayed allocations max)

compose_service.network_mode: host  (required so relayed allocations have routable ports)

reused_libraries.name: simple-peer
reused_libraries.why: Wraps RTCPeerConnection + signaling-protocol-agnostic SDP/ICE event stream. Eliminates ~300 LOC of boilerplate per side. Battle-tested.

reused_libraries.name: coturn
reused_libraries.why: Reference STUN/TURN implementation. Do not implement TURN.

reused_libraries.name: ws
reused_libraries.why: Smallest correct Node WebSocket server. No socket.io needed — we don't want rooms, namespaces, or polling fallback.

reused_libraries.name: express
reused_libraries.why: Only for routing /health, /ice-config, and static serving. Could be replaced with raw http but express keeps the code small.

env_vars_server.name: PAIR_SECRET_A
env_vars_server.purpose: Long random string identifying peer A

env_vars_server.name: PAIR_SECRET_B
env_vars_server.purpose: Long random string identifying peer B

env_vars_server.name: TURN_STATIC_AUTH_SECRET
env_vars_server.purpose: Shared between signaling server and coturn for REST-API credential minting

env_vars_server.name: PUBLIC_TURN_HOST
env_vars_server.purpose: Hostname clients should use to reach TURN (e.g. ngrok TCP tunnel hostname, or eventual prod hostname)

ngrok_dev_recipe: ngrok http 8080  -> gives https://<id>.ngrok-free.app for signaling + static client
ngrok tcp 3478   -> gives tcp://<host>:<port> for TURN (set PUBLIC_TURN_HOST/PORT to this)
Send each peer their personal link: https://<id>.ngrok-free.app/#k=<their-secret>

media_permissions.denied: If getUserMedia rejects with NotAllowedError, show centered message: 'duo needs camera and mic to work.' with a single 'try again' button that re-invokes acquireLocalStream. Do not attempt to connect signaling without media.
media_permissions.missing_device: NotFoundError -> 'No camera or mic detected.' — still allow joining audio-only if mic exists; gracefully fall back.

nat_traversal_failures.ice_failed: When iceconnectionstate transitions to 'failed', initiator calls pc.restartIce() once. If still 'failed' after 10s, set phase='failed' and show 'Couldn't connect. Both of you need to be on the same kind of network or the TURN server needs to be reachable.'
nat_traversal_failures.turn_unreachable: If iceConfig fetch fails 3x in a row, proceed with STUN-only (degraded — works for ~85% of NAT pairs). Show subtle 'TURN unavailable — direct only' in footer.

concurrency_third_party.rule: If a third valid auth attempt arrives for an already-occupied slot, the new socket replaces the old (handles laptop-sleep-then-resume). The displaced socket receives ErrorMsg{code:'replaced'} and is closed with 4000.
concurrency_third_party.rationale: Without this, transient reconnects would leave ghost slots and lock out the real user.

auth_attacks.brute_force: Server applies token-bucket rate limit on /signal upgrade attempts and /ice-config requests: 5 attempts / minute / IP, then 429 for 5 minutes. Failed-auth log line includes IP but never the presented secret.
auth_attacks.timing: auth.identifyPeer compares both pair secrets in constant time even on the negative branch (compare against both A and B, OR the results) — never short-circuits on first-byte mismatch.

input_validation.envelope_size_cap: 16 KiB per WebSocket message (server enforces; close 1009 on violation).
input_validation.schema_validation: Every incoming envelope passes Zod parse; malformed -> ErrorMsg{code:'malformed'} and counts toward rate limit.
input_validation.signal_payload_passthrough: signal.data is forwarded opaquely. The threat is bounded because the recipient is simple-peer, which only consumes well-formed SDP/ICE. A malicious peer could only attack a peer they've already authenticated as the other half of — i.e. the trusted partner. Acceptable.

xss_csrf.spa_csp: Server responds to / with Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; media-src 'self' blob:; connect-src 'self' wss: https:; img-src 'self' data:; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; frame-ancestors 'none'.
xss_csrf.csrf: No cookie-based auth -> no CSRF surface. Bearer secret is read by JS only from URL fragment or localStorage.

tls.dev: ngrok terminates TLS for HTTPS+WSS. coturn uses TURNS only if cert provided; otherwise TURN over TCP is acceptable since media is already SRTP-encrypted.
tls.prod: Front signaling-server with a reverse proxy (Caddy) for automatic Let's Encrypt; coturn loads the same cert via mounted volume.

secret_leakage.url_fragment_preferred: Pair secrets are delivered via URL fragment so they're never sent to the server in the Referer header or appear in HTTP access logs.
secret_leakage.history_scrub: Client immediately calls history.replaceState({}, '', location.pathname) after reading the fragment.
secret_leakage.logs: Server-side logger has an allowlist on what gets logged — secret values are never in the allowlist and are stripped by a recursive sanitizer before any log line is emitted.

denial_of_service.single_pair_implication: Because only one pair exists, server resource limits are extremely tight: 2 WS connections, ~100 msg/s each, 4 TURN allocations total. Anything beyond is dropped.
denial_of_service.ip_throttle: Combined with auth rate-limit above, this makes the service uninteresting as a DoS target.

browser_compat.supported: Latest 2 versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari (iOS Safari 15.4+ for getUserMedia in PWA).
browser_compat.ios_quirks: Safari requires user-gesture before getUserMedia; bootstrap must run from a click handler on first load.
browser_compat.autoplay: Remote video element is muted=false but audio playback may be blocked until user interaction; show 'tap to unmute' overlay if HTMLMediaElement.play() rejects.

presence_race.scenario: Both peers connect within ms of each other. Both could try to be initiator.
presence_race.resolution: Initiator is deterministic: slot A is ALWAYS the initiator. Slot B waits for offer. This eliminates the race entirely — no glare handling needed.

ice_restart_loop.guard: Limit ICE restarts to 3 per 60 seconds. Beyond that, surface 'failed' and require explicit user action — prevents pathological networks from burning battery.

shutdown.server: On SIGTERM, send ErrorMsg{code:'server-shutdown'} to both sockets, close cleanly with 1001, then exit. Clients auto-reconnect when server returns.

testing_strategy.scope_note: Test coverage is intentionally narrow — the surface is small and most behavior is in third-party libs.
server: unit: auth.identifyPeer correctness + timing-safety against known good/bad secrets
unit: envelope.parse rejects oversize / wrong-shape messages
unit: pairState bump-on-reconnect semantics (replaced flag, idempotent detach)
integration: spin up server, open two ws clients with valid creds, verify offer/answer relay end-to-end (using a fake SignalMsg payload)
client: manual e2e: two-browser, same-LAN -> expect 'direct'; one peer on cellular tether forcing relay -> expect 'relayed'

out_of_scope_for_v1_explicit: Push notifications when the other peer comes online
Mobile app shell (PWA install works but no native wrapper)
End-to-end identity verification beyond the pre-shared secret (SAS / safety numbers)
future_extensibility_notes: Adding text chat = one more SignalEnvelope variant ('chat', {text}) routed through the same relay path. ~20 LOC.
Adding screen share = simple-peer.addStream a second MediaStream; triggers renegotiation automatically. UI toggle only.
Push-on-online = add Web Push subscription endpoint to signaling server; broadcast on PairState attach. Stays consistent with no-database stance by storing subscription JSON in a single flat file.
